name: 1.1 Definitions of Statistics, Probability, and Key Terms

questions.title: Identifying the population of a study — the entire group under study — and distinguishing it from an overly broad group, a wrong-subject group, and a sample (§1.1.2, Definitions 1.1.4–1.1.5).

Approval Poll Key Terms (Proportion) - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a study measuring the proportion of voters who approve of a politician
Ski Lesson Age Key Terms - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a study of the mean age at a first ski or snowboard lesson
Cardiologist Recovery Key Terms - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a study of the mean recovery period after a heart attack
Insurance Health Costs Key Terms - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a study of the mean yearly health costs of an insurer's clients

Marriage Counseling Key Terms (Proportion) - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a study measuring the proportion of a counselor's clients who stay married

Ballot Measure Poll Key Terms (Proportion) - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a poll estimating the proportion of eligible voters who will vote for a local ballot measure

Product Launch Survey Key Terms (Proportion) - Match population, sample, parameter, statistic, variable, and data to their descriptions in a marketing study estimating the proportion of people in an area who will buy a new product
Classify X as the Variable - Name what X is when X is defined as a measurement on one member of the population
Sample Mean Is a Statistic - Classify a mean computed from a sample
